Pipeline/Hub.php#Hub#__construct.note: Body matches (assign the optional container). Dismissed: @Inject(ContainerContract) on the parameter is the port's spelling of PHP's reflected ?Container type hint -- owed because the provider registers singleton(PipelineHubContract, Hub) class-as-concrete; the parameter property replaces the explicit $this->container assignment.

Pipeline/Hub.php#Hub#getContainer.note: Verbatim property return. Dismissed: typed Container | undefined -- upstream's docblock claims Container but the method returns null when none was passed; the port's type states the same behavior honestly.

Pipeline/Hub.php#Hub#pipeline.note: Matches. Dismissed: PHP's keyed array becomes OrderedMap.set -- the port's standing representation for PHP associative arrays (Container, Router, LogManager and a dozen others); only keyed get/set are used here, so the choice is unobservable.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#__constru.note: Body matches; container optional as upstream, parameter property replaces the explicit assignment. Dismissed: no @Inject here, deliberately -- upstream never container-resolves Pipeline (the provider binds 'pipeline' through a closure), so no hint is owed; adding one would be surface upstream does not have.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#finally.note: Verbatim. The $finally property lives as _finally under the underscore convention (property/method name collision in one Luau table); the comparator matches it automatically.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#getContai.note: Verbatim: guard, RuntimeException with upstream's exact message, return.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#handleCar.note: Verbatim identity hook. Its call site sits inside the pcall-protected region in carry(), matching upstream's try -- the shape the earlier carry() bug was about.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#handleExc.note: Verbatim rethrow; throw e compiles to error(e), so the original pcall error value propagates unchanged.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#parsePipe.note: The string path is upstream's: first ':' splits name from ','-separated parameters, preserving explode-limit-2 semantics ('a:b:c' keeps 'b:c' as one comma-split tail). Dismissed additions: the [Class, ...args] head and the non-string pass-through exist because a class cannot be spelled inside a string on this platform -- same parameter syntax, different carrier, documented in the method docblock.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#pipe.note: Same expression as through(): is_array($pipes) ? $pipes : func_get_args() is a rest parameter plus the same ternary over isPipeArray. Dismissed: array_push's spread becomes an append loop -- roblox-ts's push macro rejects spread arguments (roblox-ts#1149), verified by the compile error.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#pipes.note: Verbatim; the $pipes property is _pipes under the underscore convention (collides with this method's name in one Luau table).

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#prepareDe.note: Same shape: the destination runs inside the protected region and a failure routes to handleException with the original passable. Dismissed: an explicit pcall instead of try/catch -- roblox-ts compiles try to TS.try over pcall anyway, and the raw error value reaches handleException either way; the port spells the pcall out because it needs the [ok, result] pair as an expression.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#then.note: Same onion, same try/finally with the same guard on _finally. Dismissed: (1) array_reduce(array_reverse(...)) becomes a backwards fold loop -- roblox-ts arrays have reduce but no reverse and no reduceRight, so the reversed reduce cannot be spelled directly; (2) with the reduce forced out, carry() takes (stack, pipe) directly instead of returning a reducer closure (carry itself is left unproposed for a separate finding, see review report); (3) the withinTransaction branch is omitted together with the withinTransaction waiver -- no database to open a transaction on; (4) the accumulator is named stack, the name upstream's carry() closure gives the same value, rather than $pipeline.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#thenRetur.note: Verbatim: then() with the identity destination.

Pipeline/Pipeline.php#Pipeline#through.note: Verbatim shape: is_array($pipes) ? $pipes : func_get_args() maps to a rest parameter and the same ternary, with isPipeArray as the platform's is_array for pipes -- it additionally tells one parameterized pipe [Class, 'args'] from a list (a class is not a string here) and recognizes the empty list Util.isArray cannot see (Pipeline/helpers.ts documents both). Even the pathological through([a], b) drops the extras like PHP does. Known heuristic edge remains for the single-array form ([ClassPipe, 'bindingName'] reads as one parameterized pipe); the restored variadic form is the unambiguous spelling of that case.

Pipeline/PipelineServiceProvider.php#Pip.note: Verbatim, same order: [PipelineHubContract, 'pipeline']; the import alias mirrors upstream's use Hub as PipelineHubContract.

Line-for-line, argument breaks included: singleton(PipelineHubContract, Hub) keeps the interface-as-key via the Contract token and class-as-concrete (Hub declares its dependency with @Inject); bind('pipeline', (app) => new Pipeline(app)) receives the resolving container as the closure parameter, mirroring fn ($app) -- no captured registering container, so per-request sandboxes stay isolated. This file is the component etalon.
